description: Seed data of the derivability knowledge graph, persistently reused across analysis tasks. When first analyzing a new functional domain, first search this file for reusable nodes / edges, then add new findings. Any added or modified edge must go through the confirmation-and-protection flow of SKILL.md Step 13; an analysis task must never silently rewrite this file. schemaVersion 1.1 introduces informationUnits: nodes that are deterministic functions of one another (zero conditional entropy) are explicitly grouped into one information unit, for direct use by section 1.1 "closure expansion and information-unit folding" of equivalence-path-validation-methodology.md, so that several derived representations of the same information are not double-counted when computing the equivalence degree.

nodes.label: Beacon (iBeacon format) UUID + major + minor + RSSI
generic BLE device raw advertisement packet (manufacturer data byte segment + RSSI + device name / identifier)

informationUnits.label: location identity information unit
informationUnits.rationale: city_id / city_name are both deterministic functions of precise_latlng (via reverse geocoding): H(city_id | precise_latlng) = H(city_name | precise_latlng) = 0, so they carry no information independent of precise_latlng and are folded into one information unit. A observed misuse: without folding, counting the literal fields of {precise latlng, city id, city name} vs {precise latlng} yields EquivDegree = 0.33; after folding the correct result is close to 1.0. See section 1.1 of equivalence-path-validation-methodology.md

informationUnits.label: iBeacon core information unit
informationUnits.rationale: this unit can itself be obtained by locally parsing device.generic_ble_advertis_data according to the iBeacon manufacturer data format (see the corresponding edge below), so the closure of the generic BLE scanning path naturally covers this unit; the closure of the Beacon-specific API path is limited to this unit and cannot cover generic_ble_advertis_data in reverse (lossy post-processing, irreversible)

edges.transform: different carrier paths of the same attribute (after calling <map-writer-API> with no arguments, <map-reader-API> reads the map center point; <screen-coord-API> with the viewport center pixel coordinate reads the same value) — if the map center has already been aligned to the user real location through a legitimate authorization flow, the two should numerically point to the same coordinate
edges.notes: a candidate member of an equivalence set built from a write-then-read composition (belongs to unit.loc_identity); not yet validated by the Step 10/11 TOST empirical tests, so errorBound.value remains to be filled in from measurement; the current evidenceStrength is based on line-by-line code evidence (state-coupling logic in the framework bundle), not empirical confirmation

edges.transform: the city code field returned by reverse geocoding

edges.notes: a constituent edge of unit.loc_identity; it illustrates that even if the direct return value of a path contains no city_id field, as long as the precise latlng is obtainable, city_id is still inside its derivable closure, so non-equivalence must not be concluded merely from a "missing field"

edges.transform: the city name field returned by reverse geocoding

resourceCost.requiresThirdPartyService: reverse geocoding service (e.g. Tencent Maps / Amap API)

edges.transform: lookup in a city code mapping table (each platform / map vendor usually maintains this static mapping)
edges.notes: city id and city name are near-lossless bidirectional mappings of each other, further confirming that both belong to the same information unit as the precise latlng, rather than being counted independently

edges.transform: coordinate quantization / truncation (reducing decimal precision or adding a random offset)
edges.sourceAnalysis: location-info-class API analysis - 20260901 (Step 7 documentation-code cross validation: the concrete strength of the <fuzzy-locate-API> fuzzing algorithm lacks quantified documentation and code evidence)
edges.notes: an example of a directed lossy edge: precise -> fuzzy holds, the reverse (fuzzy_latlng -> precise_latlng) does not, so the reverse edge must not be registered in the graph

edges.transform: call the same path k times consecutively, take the spherical distance (Haversine) between two adjacent coordinates divided by the call time difference, and differentiate numerically to estimate speed

temporal.deltaT: 2-5 s recommended; must be smaller than the path own cache / throttle window

edges.sourceAnalysis: verification-scenario generation: innovations and challenges - 20260902 (a temporal-derivability example proposed at the methodology design stage, not empirically validated)
edges.notes: an example of a temporal derivability edge: for a path that returns only coordinates and no speed field, if consecutive calls are allowed, its derivable closure may still cover the speed attribute under the sampling strategy (k=2, deltaT); the errorBound of this edge must be filled in after the Step 11 empirical test (TOST comparing this path numerical differentiation result with the speed field declared by <baseline-locate-API>); it is currently an assumption awaiting validation

edges.transform: look up coordinates against a third-party WiFi geolocation database (indoor positioning)

resourceCost.requiresThirdPartyService: third-party WiFi geolocation database (e.g. vendor WiFi positioning services)

edges.sourceAnalysis: location-info-class API analysis - 20260901 (pattern D1 cross-functional-domain substitute channel: <wifi-scan-API> and <baseline-locate-API> share the <scope-id> scope group)
edges.notes: an example of a cross-functional-domain derivable edge — used to support quantitative validation of the pattern D1 "different review criteria" equivalence channel

edges.transform: parse the advertisement packet locally according to the iBeacon protocol manufacturer data byte format (prefix + UUID + major + minor + measured power); no external service needed

errorBound.unit: none (a format match means deterministic parsing; a mismatch means the device is not an iBeacon)

edges.sourceAnalysis: verification-scenario generation: innovations and challenges - 20260902 (a hardware-scanning equivalence example proposed at the methodology design stage, not empirically validated)
edges.notes: corresponds to the example in section 4.4 of equivalence-path-validation-methodology.md: through this edge, the closure of generic BLE scanning (e.g. <ble-scan-API>) covers all core fields of the Beacon-specific API (<beacon-API>), forming a one-sided superset relation delta(Beacon -> generic BLE scanning) = empty set; the reverse does not hold — the Beacon API filters and parses at the system layer, losing non-iBeacon device information and the raw bytes, which is lossy post-processing and irreversible
